root_cause_diagnosis: 1. Severe Tree Memorization: With 3,197 raw continuous flux features and unconstrained depth, individual decision trees memorize the specific flux timestamps of the 37 positive training stars, achieving 100% predicted probability on training positives. 2. Lack of Temporal Invariance: Exoplanet transits occur at arbitrary phases/epochs. Decision trees splitting on raw timestamp columns (FLUX.k) cannot generalize to test stars whose transits occur at different times. 3. Tree Vote Dilution: Because positive examples represent only 0.73% of the data, the ensemble's average probability output on unseen test exoplanets peaks at only 0.06 (6%), never crossing the default 0.50 threshold.
